files.description: Bike-share riders, one per row (400 rows): rider_id (six-digit id with leading zeros), display_name (person name, some with accented letters), home_district (one of 6 districts such as "Old Town"), membership (casual, monthly or annual) - these three text columns have inconsistent capital letters and stray spaces; joined_on (date as text, YYYY-MM-DD; about 2% empty), birth_year (whole number; about 4% empty), credit_balance (two decimals, can be negative; about 5% empty).

task_text: Build a wide table from riders.csv with one column per home district. Each column lists the birth_year values of that district's riders from the top, in file order: row 0 holds the district's first rider, row 1 its second, and so on. A rider with an empty birth_year keeps its place as an empty cell, and a district with fewer riders than the largest one is filled up with empty cells at the bottom. `result` should be that table, with as many rows as the largest district has riders.
intended_computation: Read riders.csv; one column per home district, where a district is either home_district stripped and lower-cased (the 6 districts of the fixture) or the home_district value as written, both readings accepted; columns in any order; column d lists the birth_year values of the riders of d in file order from row 0 (empty birth_year kept as a missing cell), padded at the bottom with missing cells to as many rows as the largest district has riders.

acceptable_variants.notes: values may be float or nullable integers; the index may be 0..n-1 or unnamed; the columns may come in any order; the district columns may be the stripped, lower-cased districts or the home_district values as written (LR27)

intent_summary: Turn a long table of category and value into a wide table with one column per category, each column listing that category's values from the top in their original order, shorter columns padded with missing values.
